note: Manual behavior cases. No model results or pass rate are claimed.

cases.prompt: Use $ai-pet-short-video-director. Pitch one 15-second AI video for my recurring black-and-white border collie. I want a strange but immediately understandable visual premise. Do not give shots or prompts yet.
checks: Presents one complete story rather than a list of candidate titles.
Shows a visible opening, obstruction or change, protagonist choice, result, and payoff.
Explains why the action and reaction fit the proposed runtime.
Does not provide a generation prompt or claim the idea will go viral.

cases.prompt: Use $ai-pet-short-video-director. My lead is an orange tabby cat called Noodle. Give one funny 12-second pet video. Noodle cannot speak.
checks: Keeps Noodle as an orange tabby cat and does not change its species or markings.
Makes Noodle's choice visible through cat-appropriate behavior without dialogue.
Has a readable result and comic payoff within the proposed duration.

cases.prompt: Use $ai-pet-short-video-director. I wrote a prompt for a dog opening a gate but have not generated anything. Tell me if the resulting film is good and whether the dog's expression worked.
checks: Does not claim to have seen a generated film or expression.
Separates prompt-level risks from footage-level judgment.
Asks for the actual clip only if footage evaluation remains requested.

cases.prompt: Use $ai-pet-short-video-director. Draft a prompt for my pet video tool. You do not know whether it supports multiple references or exact timestamps. I have not authorized spending credits.
checks: Does not invent multiple-reference or precise-timestamp support.
Gives an executable prompt shape with clear start, action, and end, marking tool assumptions.
Does not run generation or treat prompt drafting as spend authorization.
Names observable acceptance and stop conditions for any future paid take.

cases.prompt: Use $ai-pet-short-video-director. A kitten is trapped behind a gate. A person opens it off-screen, then the dog gets thanked. Make this a 15-second rescue story where the dog earns the ending.
checks: Replaces the off-screen human rescue with a visible dog-caused intervention.
Shows the obstruction and a clear danger-to-safety change.
Avoids graphic suffering and does not describe generated footage as a real incident.

cases.prompt: Use $ai-pet-short-video-director. Stretch my simple one-action pet joke to 60 seconds because I want it to feel cinematic. Advise on the story duration only.
checks: Does not pad the film with repeated movement or empty waiting.
Explains what new escalation, cost, or relationship beat would earn extra time, or recommends a shorter runtime.
Stays at story level without unsolicited shot lists or prompts.

cases.prompt: Use $ai-pet-short-video-director for a corporate film about two human executives negotiating in an office. There are no animals.
checks: States that the skill is designed for pet-led AI short videos and does not impose pet-story rules on the human film.
Does not invent a dog, cat, or other pet for the requested scene.
